questions.question: Which of these is NOT mentioned as a layer of identity?
questions.explanation: The chapter describes personal, cultural, social, national and digital identity — not "genetic identity".

questions.question: What does it mean that literature can be both a "mirror" and a "window"?
options: It can reflect our own experiences and let us see into other people's realities
It should always be read twice
It means fiction is always autobiographical
questions.explanation: As a mirror, literature reflects our own feelings; as a window, it shows us other people's lives and builds empathy.

questions.question: Which terms belong to the "coming-of-age" theme?
options: Loss of innocence, moral growth, self-discovery
questions.explanation: Coming-of-age stories deal with loss of innocence, moral growth and self-discovery during the transition to adulthood.

questions.question: What does "code-switching" mean in the context of cultural identity?
options: Shifting between languages or styles depending on the cultural context
questions.explanation: Code-switching is when people shift between languages, dialects or styles depending on which cultural context they are in.

questions.question: What does the writing advice "show, don't tell" mean?
options: Use concrete details and actions instead of just stating feelings directly
Read your text aloud to the class
questions.explanation: "Show, don't tell" means letting details, actions and imagery convey emotions instead of simply stating them.
